deductions.observed_difference: B begins with two full frames of the dancer standing with hands on hips, while A begins already in the side-to-side dance with arms out and knees bent. These are extra/wrong poses at the start.
Several later poses in B appear phase-shifted or reordered relative to the same grid positions in A, though many of the individual dance poses are still present.
B has at least two frames where the pose is not clearly recoverable because the dancer is heavily blurred/washed out, notably around row 2 column 4 and row 3 column 6.
Wardrobe is largely faithful: shiny dark suit, white shirt, tie/suspenders are retained. Minor differences include slightly different jacket drape, sheen, and shirt/tie rendering.
The plain white studio background is mostly retained, but B has visible pale green/gray tinting and bright rectangular washout regions around the corrupted/blurred frames.
Most frames keep a similar full-body studio framing, but B has inconsistent scale/placement and two washed-out blurred frames where the figure is poorly defined or partially lost.
B preserves much of the low-budget white-background dance-video style, but the obvious generative blur/washout artifacts and initial hands-on-hips frames disrupt the original retro performance look.

uncertainty_due_to_sampled_frames: Moderate. The contact sheets sample every 1/6 second, so some in-between motion could differ unseen. However, the visible added hands-on-hips opening frames and the washed-out blurred frames are clear observed differences, so the pair is not nearly perfect.
